raw_text:
name: python-guide
Applies to Python 3.11+, APIs, CLIs, Data Pipelines, Automation.

- All function signatures, class attributes, and module-level variables must have type annotations.
- No `*` imports, no mutable default arguments, no implicit type coercions.
- Never install into system Python; use `venv`, `uv`, or `poetry`.
- Use pytest for all testing; fixtures and parametrize over setUp/tearDown.
- Enforce style mechanically; never rely on manual formatting.
- Target Python 3.11+; set `requires-python = ">=3.11"` in `pyproject.toml`; use `match`, `ExceptionGroup`, `tomllib`, and `from __future__ import annotations`.
- Never use features removed in 3.12+ (`distutils`, `imp`, legacy `typing` aliases).
- Run `ruff check` and `ruff format` before every commit. Max line length: 88 characters.
- No bare `except:` or `except Exception:` without re-raising. Catch specific exceptions. Use domain-specific exception hierarchies, `raise ... from err`, boundary logging/interior raising, `contextlib.suppress()`, and `with`/`contextlib.closing`.
- Define deps in `pyproject.toml`; pin lock-file versions; generated-only `requirements.txt`; separate optional dev/test/docs deps; audit with `pip-audit` or `safety`; prefer stdlib.
- Use src layout (`src/myproject/`), `py.typed`, root `conftest.py`, no `tests/__init__.py`; split modules at ~200 lines.
- Use `snake_case`, `PascalCase`, `UPPER_SNAKE`; `pathlib.Path`, f-strings, `collections.abc` (`Sequence`, `Mapping`, `Iterable`), `X | None`, `TypeAlias`, `Protocol`; public functions MUST have full type annotations. Use `<REDACTED_USER>` for functions returning different types based on input. Run `mypy --strict` in CI (no `type: ignore` without explanation).
- Tests: `test_*.py`, `test_<unit>_<scenario>_<expected>`; pytest functions, fixtures, `tmp_path`, parametrization, `AsyncMock`; coverage >80% business logic, >60% overall; `<REDACTED_USER>.mark.sl
